newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ABNi partner to divest stake in India TV station.
newsitem.headline: ABNi partner to divest stake in India TV station.

text.p: One of three partners in joint venture Indian television station ABNi will divest its share in the company, ABNi said on Wednesday.
It said in a statement that gave few details all matters relating to the joint venture had been settled among the partners.

IndusInd Communications Ltd (ICL) will transfer its 26 percent equity stake to Asia Business News (ABN), the statement said. It said "the parties are looking for an investor to acquire the equity portion of ICL in ABNi".

"We've had several months of quite amicable discussions. Their decision is based on differences in business projections," Paul France, ABN chief executive officer, told Reuters. He declined to say what the differences were.
ABNi, a channel which is aimed at viewers on the Indian sub-continetn, uses about 25 percent of news from ABN. Apart from ICL and ABN, the other partner in the station is India's Television Eighteen.
ABN is the majority shareholder 51 percent. Television Eighteen has a 23 percent share.
ABNi has been operating in India since December 1995. France declined to disclose its financial earnings.
